title: Repository command surface target governance
purpose: Define command-surface target taxonomy, assurance boundaries, proof expectations, dependency records, destructive-command safety, and owner-decision requirements for repository optimisation planning without changing Makefile targets, package scripts, CI, validators, proof scripts, or runtime code.

inspectedSources: AGENTS.md current preferred command entry points
USF-384 baseline timing and cost measurement
USF-427 Dev to Test to Staging ladder semantics
USF-441 policy preventing unnecessary staging promotion
USF-598 artifact inventory and retention policy
USF-633 artifact diffability and review ergonomics
currentStateRules: Current preferred aliases are workflow routers and do not upgrade readiness claims.
Compatibility aliases remain valid until a separately authorised replacement is validated.
Provider mode and environment remain separate dimensions.
Generated reports are lower authority than source evidence and semantic definitions.
Hermetic mock proof does not satisfy live external provider proof.

dependencyStatus.title: Dev to Test to Staging ladder semantics

inventorySources: AGENTS.md current preferred command entry points
existingTargetInventory.inventoryBoundary: This inventory records the current preferred and compatibility entry points relevant to command-surface redesign. Future implementation must re-check the live Makefile and package script surface before changing targets.

targetTaxonomy.purpose: Frozen dependency install and local setup routing.
targetTaxonomy.assuranceBoundary: Setup readiness only; does not prove semantic correctness, test readiness, staging suitability, or production suitability.
targetTaxonomy.validationExpectation: Future changes must preserve frozen dependency expectations and fail visibly on missing prerequisites.

targetTaxonomy.assuranceBoundary: Dev-level local confidence only; does not satisfy Test, Staging, live-provider, or human acceptance proof.
targetTaxonomy.validationExpectation: Future target changes must map outputs to assurance classes and retain escalation guidance.

targetTaxonomy.assuranceBoundary: Foundation-level repository consistency; not a product, deployment, compliance, store, production, or release claim.
targetTaxonomy.validationExpectation: Future target changes must preserve all required foundation checks or explicitly define a validator-checkable replacement.

targetTaxonomy.purpose: Bounded test-readiness command gate and composed semantic harness routing.
targetTaxonomy.assuranceBoundary: Test proof only; does not imply staging, production-live, live-provider, or human acceptance proof.
targetTaxonomy.validationExpectation: Future target changes must map Test checks to assurance classes and preserve required evidence outputs.

targetTaxonomy.purpose: Coverage, enterprise assurance, repository evidence, and bounded assurance proof routing.
targetTaxonomy.assuranceBoundary: Assurance-specific proof only; generated reports remain lower authority than underlying evidence.
targetTaxonomy.validationExpectation: Future changes must keep fail-closed semantics for stale, unknown, missing, provider-mismatched, or environment-mismatched evidence.

targetTaxonomy.purpose: Explicit staging-relevant proof when the environment ladder requires it.
targetTaxonomy.assuranceBoundary: Staging proof must not become the default for ordinary documentation, semantic, tooling, validator, cache, or Dev/Test changes.
targetTaxonomy.validationExpectation: Future implementation must cite environment-ladder policy and preserve provider-mode and environment separation.

targetTaxonomy.primaryEntryPoint: future clean, reset, explain, dry-run, and cache-clean targets
targetTaxonomy.purpose: Local maintenance and inspectability without evidence loss.
targetTaxonomy.assuranceBoundary: Maintenance output is not proof and must not delete accepted evidence or authority files by default.
targetTaxonomy.validationExpectation: Future destructive or cleanup targets must include dry-run validation, protected-path tests, and owner approval where high risk exists.

coveredIssues.title: Makefile target taxonomy and naming standard
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Target names must expose assurance level, environment relevance, provider relevance, cost, side effects, and compatibility status without treating aliases as stronger proof.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must validate target inventory, preferred aliases, compatibility aliases, and assurance mapping against command graph and assurance matrix.

coveredIssues.title: Fast local dev target
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Fast local feedback can reduce cost but must state that it is not full validation, Test proof, Staging proof, or readiness evidence.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must print included checks, excluded checks, escalation triggers, and non-claim wording.

coveredIssues.title: Dev validation target
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Dev validation must be proportionate and must not overclaim Test or Staging assurance.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must map target outputs to assurance classes and preserve escalation to Test or Staging when required.

coveredIssues.title: Test validation target
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Test validation must require proportionate tests and evidence without becoming a staging substitute.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must map Test checks to assurance classes and evidence outputs.

coveredIssues.title: Staging validation target
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Staging validation must remain explicit, limited to staging-relevant risks, and separate from default Dev or Test flows.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must cite environment ladder policy and keep production-shaped, production-live, hermetic-mock, and live-external-provider distinctions intact.

coveredIssues.title: Full proof target
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: A full proof target must preserve all required assurance and must not weaken accepted proof expectations through renaming or regrouping.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must preserve or explicitly disposition all existing proof obligations and evidence outputs.

coveredIssues.title: Changed-files and affected-only target
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Affected-only execution can reduce cost only when input classification is complete; ambiguity must fall back to fuller gates.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must prove affected-only equivalence for supported change classes and fail closed for unknown inputs.

coveredIssues.title: Explicit expensive target warnings
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Warnings improve cost visibility but must not discourage required proof or imply that expensive assurance is optional when applicable.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must preserve target exit behaviour and include non-claim wording with cost labels.

coveredIssues.title: Target help and documentation generation
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Generated help can improve discoverability but must not become semantic authority or hide compatibility paths.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must check generated documentation against target inventory, command graph, preferred aliases, and compatibility aliases.

coveredIssues.title: Idempotent targets and safe reruns
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Rerun guidance must prevent stale state from creating false passes and must prevent cleanup from deleting required evidence.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must prove rerun behaviour for changed targets and preserve stale-evidence failure behaviour.

coveredIssues.title: Target output and artifact location standard
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Output locations must preserve evidence references, generated report lower authority, artifact retention, and review workflows.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must validate artifact references, manifests, freshness markers, and generated-report source links.

coveredIssues.title: Target exit-code standard
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Exit-code normalisation must preserve fail-closed validation and proof semantics for pass, fail, blocked, skipped, unsupported, timeout, and unknown outcomes.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must include failure-path tests for changed commands and must not convert fail, stale, unknown, timeout, or blocked outcomes into pass.

coveredIssues.title: Target dependency graph generation
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: A generated graph can support affected-only checks but remains a generated report and cannot define command authority by itself.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must compare generated graph output to known command dependencies and fail closed on unresolved edges.

coveredIssues.title: Target dry-run and explain mode
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Explain output can reduce unsafe execution but must not be treated as proof execution or validation evidence.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must validate explain output against the command graph and display side effects, artifacts, proof level, environment, provider mode, and cost.

coveredIssues.title: Target environment-variable validation
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Environment-variable checks must fail closed when required inputs are missing or unsafe while avoiding unnecessary blockers for hermetic local workflows.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must include failure cases for missing, malformed, unsafe, provider-incompatible, and environment-incompatible inputs.

coveredIssues.title: Target secret and credential fail-closed checks
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Secret checks must prevent leaks, prevent credential overclaiming, and preserve hermetic workflows where live credentials are not required.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must include negative controls for missing, unsafe, exposed, or provider-incompatible credentials.

coveredIssues.title: Makefile split into modules if beneficial
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Splitting can improve maintainability but can harm execution traceability, help output, and agent instructions if target flow becomes obscure.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future split must pass full command-surface validation and preserve all targets and aliases unless separately dispositioned.
coveredIssues.ownerDecisionRequirement: Owner decision is required before splitting the Makefile or changing include strategy.

coveredIssues.title: Removal or deprecation of duplicate or superseded targets
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Removing or deprecating a target can break CI, agents, proof routes, or evidence references, so compatibility windows and disposition are required.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future implementation must run before-and-after command-equivalence validation and preserve proof routes unless explicitly dispositioned.
coveredIssues.ownerDecisionRequirement: Owner decision is required before removing, renaming, or deprecating a risky target.

coveredIssues.title: Human-safe destructive target policy
coveredIssues.assuranceImpact: Destructive targets must protect raw evidence, accepted proof, authority files, lockfiles, and credentials while still allowing explicit cleanup when safe.
coveredIssues.validationOrProofExpectation: Future destructive commands must include dry-run validation, protected-path tests, and safety tests before mutation.
coveredIssues.ownerDecisionRequirement: Owner decision is required for high-risk cleanup that could remove evidence, proof, source authority, dependency locks, or shared service state.

protectedPathsAndInputs: generated reports with unresolved source evidence
destructiveTargetDefaults: no deletion of evidence or authority files by default
owner decision required for high-risk policy changes

nonClaims: This artefact does not implement, remove, rename, split, or deprecate any Makefile target.
This artefact does not change package scripts, CI workflows, validators, proof scripts, runtime code, or generated reports.
This artefact does not approve a Makefile split, target removal, target deprecation, destructive cleanup, or staging promotion.
This artefact does not make a readiness, staging, production, compliance, store, deployment, release, or live-provider claim.
This artefact does not treat generated command documentation or dependency graphs as semantic authority.
